details.description: Takes the card payment. A 429 means a rate limit, and Orders retries it.

data.text: How a checkout becomes an order and a confirmation email.

details.description: Ends TLS, checks the session cookie with Auth and routes /orders to the Orders service.
Validates the cart, charges the card through Stripe, writes the order and publishes order.created.

steps.caption: The shopper presses Pay.
The gateway checks the session and routes the request.
Orders validates the cart.
Stripe rate-limits the first charge, so Orders retries it.
The retry succeeds.
Orders writes the order row in one transaction.
The row is committed.
Orders publishes order.created.
The email worker sends the confirmation.
The web SDK sends a batch of events.
The collector checks the schema and adds a receive time.
Kafka keeps the batch on 12 partitions.
Two consumer groups read the same events at the same time.
The enricher adds user and geo data while fraud scoring rates each event.
Analysts can query the events within five minutes.
A score above 0.9 pages the on-call engineer.
The on-call engineer gets the alert in seconds.
A returning customer lands from a search ad.
They open the product page.
Add to cart
The cart shows two items.
The app checks the session.
The session is valid, so sign-in is skipped.
They pay with a saved wallet.
Order placed in 41 seconds.
